text:
Predicates:
SupervisedLearning(x) ::: x is a supervised learning algorithm.
UnsupervisedLearning(x) ::: x is an unsupervised learning algorithm.
ReinforcementLearning(x) ::: x is a reinforcement learning algorithm.
Trains(x, y) ::: x trains y.
Uses(x, y) ::: x uses y.
RequiresLabelling(x) ::: x requires labelled data.
Model(y) ::: y is a model.
TextSummarizationModel(y) ::: y is a text summarization model.
StateOfTheArt(y) ::: y is the state-of-the-art.
Premises:
¬(ReinforcementLearning(y) ∧ Trains(y, TextSummarizationModel)) ::: Reinforcement learning is not used to train the text summarization model.
∀x (Trains(x, TextSummarizationModel) → (SupervisedLearning(x) ∨ UnsupervisedLearning(x) ∨ ReinforcementLearning(x))) ::: The training algorithm for the model is a machine learning algorithm.
∃x (SupervisedLearning(x) ∧ Trains(x, TextSummarizationModel)) ::: There exists a supervised learning algorithm that trains the text summarization model.
RequiresLabelling(y) ::: The machine learning algorithm for training the text summarization model requires labelled data.
Conclusion:
∃x (SupervisedLearning(x) ∧ Trains(x, TextSummarizationModel)) ::: Supervised learning is used to train the model.
